topics.topic: Complete scope of retention actions and transitions that must be replayed
questions: Is this an exhaustive replay list, and does it include inverse actions such as lifting a restriction or resuming a relationship, as well as both customer erasure and project anonymisation or deletion?
Exactly which transitions must the record contain and the owner repeat, including lifting restrictions, resuming relationships, project anonymisation or deletion, and repeated or superseding actions?

quotes:
The owner first starts the restored instance owner-only (A17 rule 1), so
   no service and no agent reaches it, and brings each Customer and project to
   the state the owner's own record of the retention review (R0-60) gives for
   it now — erased, restricted, ended or not — and erases audit entries before
   the latest date the owner erased by, before configuring the tokens and
   starting it again.
judgement.why: State 2 requires restoration to the current recorded state rather than replaying every historical transition, so lifted restrictions, resumed relationships and the current erased or unerased state are covered by the final state the record gives.

topics.topic: Identity of the two recovery records referred to as either record
questions: Which two records does “either record” mean?
What are the two records meant by "either record": the export and import choices separately, an import-recovery bundle and the retention-review record, or something else?

quotes:
What the owner repeats after a restore — erasures,
restrictions, ends of a relationship, the latest date audit entries were
erased by — follows the owner's record of the retention review (R0-60): a
governance document, outside this case (Explicit exclusions), naming each
action by its date, kind and the `customer_ref` or `project_id` it touched,
with no personal value.

The kept export and the import's choices hold
personal data: the owner keeps them in the vault (R0-23), the governance
lists them as a copy that remains, as R0-81 lists the services' copies, and
the owner deletes them once a checked backup holds the import. Where either
record is missing, what the restored store holds stands until the owner
corrects it.

Until each has, the governance's records of processing list
the copies that remain, with their service and the change that removes them.
judgement.divergence: One implementation treats the two records as the retention-review record and the governance record of the retained migration copy, while another treats the export and the import choices as the two records; the owner notices because different missing information prevents or permits different recovery corrections.
judgement.why: The singular phrase “either record” has no unambiguous pair of antecedents among the retention-review record, records of processing, export file and import choices.

topics.topic: Interval of changes lost when restoring from backup
questions: Which changes are lost: changes made after the restored backup was created, changes made after its last successful check, or some other interval?
Which changes are lost: changes committed after the backup snapshot, changes made after the store was lost, or some other interval?

quotes:
The
   restored store begins its own history from the backup (R0-89): every change
   after the backup's instant is lost, the audit entries with it, and
   numbering continues from the backup's last number (A15). Being the newest,
   no kept backup is newer than it.
judgement.why: State 2 fixes the cutoff at the backup's instant.

topics.topic: Representation and cutoff-date field for audit-entry erasure without a customer or project identifier
questions: How is an audit-entry erasure represented when it touches neither a `customer_ref` nor a `project_id`, and where is its cutoff date stored?
How is an audit-entry erasure recorded when it touches neither a customer nor a project, and does its cutoff date replace the required entity identifier?

quotes:
the subject, by identity only (R0-37), one of a closed set fixed by the
  action (owner, 2026-10-31; codex round-02 T4): the project (`project_id`)
  for a project's actions; the customer (`customer_ref`) for a customer's
  actions, restricting and lifting, ending and resuming; the session and the
  project for a grant or a revocation; for the import, the digest of the file
  it accepted (M10) — the migration closure is unique in the instance and has
  no other identity (codex round-04 T1); none for an erasure of old entries,
  whose fact is the owner's date;
for an erasure of old entries: the date the owner gave (R0-66).
judgement.why: State 1 specifies that an audit-entry erasure has no entity subject and stores the owner-provided cutoff date as its own fact.

topics.topic: Whether the Bitwarden vault may hold personal-data files and the resulting hosting and recipient implications
questions: Is the R0-23 Bitwarden vault permitted and technically able to hold these files, where is it hosted, and does any vault operator or provider become a recipient of the personal data?

topics.topic: Which relevant date to record for actions with multiple dates
questions: Which date is recorded when an action has more than one relevant date, such as the execution date and an earlier relationship-end date, or the execution date and the audit-erasure cutoff?
